To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
intermittent PTH and IGF‐1 had contrasting effects on bone in aged ovariectmized rats.
PTH stimulates bone formation and that IGF‐I stimulates bone resorption and blunts the bone‐forming effects of PTH in older Ovx animals.
PTH stimulated bone growth in a manner similar in aged rats to that observed in estrogen‐replete, young adult animals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of parathyromone (PTH) and insulin‐like Growth Factor (IGF) on bone.
the role of the parathyroid hormone (PTH) in bone metabolism and the development of new therapies for osteoporosis.
the role that the parathyroid hormone (PTH)/vitamin D endocrine system plays in the control of calcium homeostasis and the regulation of bone turnover in the rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of IGF-I in older ovariectomy rats differ from those in young ovariectomy rats.
PTH and IGF‐1 have different effects on bone remodeling and bone mass.

the effects of IGF-1 in older Ovx rat models may differ from those of younger estrogen-replete animals, and that IGF-1 stimulates bone resorption and blunts the bone-forming response to PTH in older Ovx animals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
intermittent human PTH‐ (1–34) stimulates bone formation and reduces resorption and that IGF‐I stimulates bone resorption in aged Ovx rats.
PTH is the most effective agent in stimulating bone formation, and IGF‐1 is the most effective in stimulating bone resorption.

The main takeaway from our work is that
PTH and IGF‐1 have opposing effects on bone in an aged oophorectomized rat model.
IGF‐I has a negative impact on bone in an aged Ovariectomized Rat model of Postmenopausal Osteoporosis.
the anabolic effect of PTH on bone is not affected by aging and that the anabolic effects of PTH and IGF‐1 are additive in young rats but not in older rats.
